newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Crown says sub-underwriters not needed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Crown says sub-underwriters not needed.

text.p: Casino group Crown Ltd said on Tuesday its A$185 million renounceable rights issue was so popular with institutions that sub-underwriters were not needed.

Crown's major shareholders, Hudson Conway Ltd and Consolidated Press Holdings Ltd, part of media baron Kerry Packer's stable, were to have sub-underwritten the 1-for-6 issue if required by the main underwriters.
The issue is still priced at a hefty discount to the market price at A$1.80 per share, despite a steep tumble in the share price after the issue was announced.

The main underwriters, Prudential Bache Securities (Australia) Ltd and Macquarie Underwriting Ltd, have told Crown that institutional demand for the issue is strong and sub-underwriters will not be needed, the company said.
Crown's new A$2.2 billion casino and hotel complex is scheduled to open in Melbourne by early May.

Crown puts the total capital cost of the project at A$1.55 billion, but this does not include the A$150 million earmarked for a second tower nor the estimated A$300 million Crown will spend to buy back management rights to the casino operation.
The A$2.2 billion figure also includes the cost of Crown's A$200 million exclusive licence, which had been included in the company's original cost estimates before expanding the project.
